notes:
**CHR-1257 phase 2a, Stitch chrome (2026-11-27, awaiting Christian's approval).** The chrome stays light; the user's own screen inside the frame is dark (literal colours, it stands for someone else's design). The read highlight (teal, solid) on the Visitors card and the write highlight (violet, dashed, wash) on the Revenue card are `activity-highlight` instances sized to the node; both stay readable on the dark content. Highlights inside the frame keep their theme-independent tokens (decision `chr905-c-rollout-details`).

---
Earlier notes (history):

CHR-628/CHR-629: proves the read/write highlight tokens hold up over a dark-content mock — `screen-frame`, `frame-bar` and the card backgrounds here use literal dark colors (#14151a / #1f2029 / #2a2c35) rather than design-system tokens, since this frame represents an arbitrary dark-themed screen someone else designed, not our own tool's chrome (which has no dark mode). `$color.activity-read` (teal) and `$color.activity-write` (violet) were picked to read clearly against both light and dark surfaces without needing separate dark-mode variants of the highlight itself.
